extracted.intended_audience: Bona fide Media Organisations (accredited and non-accredited written press, photographers, non-rights-holding broadcasters, and other rights-holding media) reporting on the Olympic Games
extracted.subtask_description: Official IOC guidelines for how media organisations may reproduce and refer to Olympic trademarks, marks, terminology, imagery and related content in editorial news reporting, including special rules for non-rights-holding broadcasters and digital/social use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: protection of the Olympic Properties and the Olympic Movement
rubrics_metrics.description: The IOC must ensure that the integrity and value of the Olympic Properties are respected; protection is critical to the viability of the Olympic Movement and is protected by specific legislation and/or Intellectual Property Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media Organisations should use each Olympic Property in accordance with its own context (e.g., Olympic Qualifier Series brand for Qualifiers). The IOC recognizes the media role but reserves protection and enforcement rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior written approval required for uses not expressly permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: For any use of the Olympic Properties not expressly permitted in the Guidelines, prior written approval from the IOC is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact legal@olympic.org for approval. For editorial uses, ring graphics may be requested at images@olympic.org. For OCOG and NOC graphics, contact the respective Organising Committee or National Olympic Committee via the provided IOC links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of the Olympic Properties (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Olympic Properties (rings, emblems, wordmarks, Look of the Games, mascots, pictograms, motto, etc.) must be maintained and must not be altered, distorted, or used out of context or in pieces not relevant to the Olympic Games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes preservation of visual form and oral terminology integrity; oral mentions should follow the Official Terminology list provided by the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred version of the Olympic rings
rubrics_metrics.description: The full-colour version on its white background is the preferred version of the Olympic rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monochrome rings provide an alternative where needed; the rings may appear in any of the six official Olympic colours when necessary, but the full-colour-on-white is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on altering the Olympic rings (alterations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Olympic rings should never be altered in any way, including modifying the official colours or the order of the colours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of prohibited alterations include reordering colours, changing colours, inserting imagery, placing graphics in front/through/behind the rings, flipping horizontally, and rotating in 3D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation requirement for the Olympic rings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Olympic rings must always be reproduced horizontally, with three rings on top and two on the bottom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not flip the rings horizontally or rotate them; maintain the canonical arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background rules for Olympic rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Backgrounds must ensure maximum visibility of the Olympic rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-colour rings must be placed on white background. For monochrome use, the background must be consistent behind the rings. Do not place rings on backgrounds that create gaps at intersections or distort visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on visual distortions of the Olympic rings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Olympic rings must always be visible in their entirety and should never be distorted in any way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not stretch, deform, distort width, reproduce rings as objects/shapes/people/products, insert images/words/illustrations into the rings, or apply rings onto surfaces where their shape is distorted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral integrity of Olympic terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Olympic terminology, when orally referred, cannot be altered or distorted, or used in a way that is not relevant to the piece or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Official Terminology list provided in the Guidelines; a non-exhaustive list of acceptable terms is given (e.g., Olympic Games, Olympiad, Olympic flame, Olympic Village, Olympism, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial use allowed only for legitimate news reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Organisations may reproduce the Olympic Properties solely in an editorial context within their publication for legitimate news reporting purposes to provide factual reference and information on the Olympic Games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Olympic Properties may be used to illustrate news stories related to the Olympic Games but must remain within editorial reporting contexts (not promotional or commercial contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on commercial use or promotional association
rubrics_metrics.description: The Olympic Properties must not be used for commercial or corporate purposes, in advertising, taglines, slogans or otherwise in any form of commercial content to promote any entity, brand, product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes preventing any impression of official or non-official association with the IOC, OCOGs, the Olympic Movement, or Olympic Partners; applies to Media Organisations themselves and third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: No implication of official or formal association
rubrics_metrics.description: The Olympic Properties must not be used in a way that suggests a formal or official association between Media Organisations (or third parties) and the IOC, OCOGs, the Olympic Games, or the Olympic Movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid usage in advertorials, promotional campaigns, or any context that could create the impression of endorsement, selection, approval, warranty, preference or consent by the IOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography: use of accredited photographers' images
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs taken by accredited photographers at the Olympic Games and available from news agencies or accredited photographers may be used by Media Organisations for reporting purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use photographs to create an unauthorised association or for commercial/promotional purposes (including promoting the Media Organisation). Any still-image use that simulates moving imagery (e.g., GIF animations) is strictly prohibited. See Photographers’ Undertaking for related obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio-Visual content restrictions and News Access Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Media organisations may not film within Olympic venues. Non-Rights-Holding Broadcasters' use of Olympic audiovisual content is limited to the terms and conditions of the News Access Rules of the respective Olympic Games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moving images are governed by the News Access Rules; non-RHBs must adhere to specific access and use restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain names and social media accounts rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Organisations are not allowed to create specific Olympic-related websites or social media accounts using Olympic Properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may create a section dedicated to the Olympic Games within the official website or social media account of the Media Organisation (e.g., www.medianame.com/olympicgames or social media.com/medianame/olympicgames are acceptable; separate Olympic-specific domain/account like medianameolympicgames.com is not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media content permitted practices (limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: For social media content creation, certain practices are allowed provided the overall principles are observed and no association with third-party advertisers is created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed: Hash tagging using Olympic Properties (e.g., #OlympicGames, #Olympics); visual posts using verbal references to the Olympic Properties; creation of Instagram temporary/permanent stories using verbal references. Prohibited: using Olympic Properties alongside brand sponsorship posts that imply association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application (app) restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: If reporting via an application, reporting must be done through the Media Organisation's existing general application with a dedicated Olympic section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Olympic rings and the emblem cannot be used in the app icon; the app name cannot contain 'Olympic / Olympics / Olympic Games / Olympiad' or equivalents; the app's graphic identity must not suggest endorsement or official status (e.g., avoid using Rings Colours or Look of the Games or any derivation or colourable imitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastheads and footers prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Olympic Properties must not be incorporated into the mastheads or footers of a publication or screen view page of a website and/or social media account, to avoid implying a false association with the IOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to use Olympic Properties to illustrate Olympic coverage provided this is separate from the original masthead or footer bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship, advertisements and promotions on editorial pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party advertisements or promotions on an editorial-content page related to the Olympic Games are permitted, but sponsorship of Olympic content is not allowed unless by an Olympic Partner with prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising must remain clearly distinct and separate from editorial pieces and Olympic Properties; avoid overlapping, intrusive, or superimposed adverts on editorial reproduction/presentation. Media Organisations must not present themselves as official/approved partners nor sell sponsorship opportunities tied to Olympic Properties without IOC approval. 'Presentation and impression will be key.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Olympic Games supplements rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplements or special editions devoted to Olympic coverage are permitted but must avoid giving the false impression of being an official or authorised IOC publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplements must not be sponsored by companies other than Olympic Partners without prior written approval. Same advertising/sponsorship rules apply. A full takeover of advertising space offering exclusivity is not permitted as it may imply official association. IOC authorizes periodical newsletters if Guidelines are respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Olympic features (countdown clocks, medal tables) allowed if unbranded
rubrics_metrics.description: Unbranded information features (e.g., countdown clocks and medal tables) may be used to illustrate Olympic reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their implementation is subject to the same principles in the Guidelines, including rules on advertisements and sponsorship (no unauthorised sponsored branding unless approved).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing links to official IOC websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to official IOC websites are accepted provided the link is formatted in plain text only, does not use Olympic Properties, and is not associated with sponsorship, advertising, or third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present links in a way that uses Olympic marks or that connects the link to third-party commercial messaging; keep link text plain (e.g., olympics.com).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contests, games and lotteries prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Organisations must not use the Olympic Properties in any contest, game, or lottery, or to promote special offers for subscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media Organisations must not raffle tickets or hospitality services for the Olympic Games as prizes. Avoid promotional competitions that reference Olympic Properties or imply Olympic affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Rights-Holding Broadcasters: limited on-screen use
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Rights-Holding Broadcasters may use Olympic Properties on-screen for illustration editorial purposes solely while specifically reporting on the Olympic Games (not in general sports/news programmes), and subject to limitations on following pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-RHBs must comply with additional IOC guidelines: News Access Rules for the relevant edition and IOC Social and Digital Media Guidelines for accredited persons. Use is restricted to specific Olympic reporting segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcaster bug and/or logo prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Rights-Holding Broadcasters must not create a network bug with any Olympic properties, nor create a composite logo with any Olympic Property or use Olympic Properties in a logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bugs or on-screen logos that incorporate Olympic marks are forbidden as they imply rights-holding or official status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network branding prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Rights-Holding Broadcasters must not display any Olympic Properties on network branding (e.g., microphones, uniforms, pins) — inside or outside the studio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid any physical branding that includes Olympic marks on personnel or equipment to prevent impression of rights-holding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studio layout and backdrop restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Rights-Holding Broadcasters must not decorate the studio with Olympic Properties or create an Olympic logo, and must not report with Olympic event or venue footage in the background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using Olympic event footage in studio backdrops (live or delayed) would give the impression of being Rights-Holding Broadcasters. Use of moving images remains subject to News Access Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming of programmes prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Rights-Holding Broadcasters must not use the Olympic Properties for the naming of a programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programme titles should not include Olympic marks or imply an official Olympic programme (e.g., avoid 'Olympic Coverage' as part of the programme name if it implies association).

rubrics_metrics.name: No sponsorship of Olympic content (NRHB-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsorship of Olympic content or its reproduction or presentation is not permitted for Non-Rights-Holding Broadcasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRHBs must not seek or display sponsorship connected with Olympic content; Olympic Partners may be permitted only with prior written approval of the IOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and consequences for breach
rubrics_metrics.description: Any breach of these Guidelines will be reviewed by the IOC, and appropriate action will be taken, including, if necessary, the withdrawal of accreditation at the Games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media Organisations should treat the Guidelines as mandatory operational restrictions; non-compliance risks accreditation loss and other enforcement measures.
